newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: EDP wants Telecel stake but stock too high.
newsitem.headline: EDP wants Telecel stake but stock too high.

text.p: Portuguese state electricity concern EDP said it was in talks to take a 20 percent stake in mobile phone operator Telecel but added it was not prepared to buy at the current share price which was too high.
"We began formal talks last week with Air Touch and Telepri," EDP chairman Antonio de Almeida said.
The European subsidiary of U.S. Air Touch recently bought a controlling stake in the the mobile phone operator from Portuguese consortium Telepri. Some 40 percent of Telecel is quoted on the market.
De Almeida said that the electricity concern was only interested in entering into the shareholding of Telecel if it were guaranteed a stake of 20 percent.
"But at the current stock price, we are not going to do anything," he told a news conference.
Telecel stock has soared to a high of 11,800 escudos per share since being floated at 7,950 escudos in early September.
It was trading at 11,701 escudos on Friday.
De Almeida said that the negotiations on EDP taking a stake would probably take six months.
The news conference had been called to give details of the plans of three state-owned energy companies, including EDP, to study jointly the possibility of entering the telecommunications business.
